clue.text: Cock-a-hoop? Quite the reverse!

parts.note: cock-a-hoop means jubilant, so its reverse is a dejected state; the image is also of a cockerel whose comb has drooped

explanation.surface: Someone says 'cock-a-hoop?' and answers that the truth is the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Cock-a-hoop literally evokes a crowing cock; the opposite picture is a cock whose crest has dropped, the literal sense of the dejected word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dejected and disappointed is the opposite of jubilant, which is what cock-a-hoop means.

clue.text: Rule by restraint, not force

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Rule by restraint, not force (5)' for REIGN: restraint gives REIN, but no clue word supplies the G, and 'not force' gives no letters or operation in any reading found

clue.text: Nordic limited edition with de luxe cover

indicators.note: the de luxe word acts as a cover wrapped round the edition piece, so it goes on the outside

parts.note: swish means smart, luxurious, de luxe
edition cut short, limited, gives its abbreviation ED

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian book appears as a limited edition in a luxurious binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited edition' reads as a collector's phrase, but 'limited' only means the word is cut short; 'cover' says the de luxe word wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedish is an adjective for things from Sweden, one of the Nordic countries.

clue.text: Former dictator takes her dancing, swathed in ermine?

indicators.note: the scrambled pronoun is wrapped inside the fur piece, as a dancer might be swathed in a stole

parts.note: ermine is a white fur, an example of fur, hence the question mark

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the three letters of her are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former tyrant takes a woman out dancing, she dressed in ermine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' scrambles the pronoun to HRE and 'swathed in' wraps the fur round it; the question mark admits ermine is just one kind of fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was Hitler's as leader of Nazi Germany, a dictator now in the past.

clue.text: Strange bait swallowed by cat — an offering of wine

indicators.note: the jumbled bait disappears inside the big cat as if eaten

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of bait come out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A cat gulps down odd bait, followed by a ritual pouring of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' scrambles the bait to BATI, and 'swallowed by' hides it inside the big cat; 'cat' tempts toward a pet, but it is a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is a drink poured out in honour of a god, typically wine.

clue.text: One last dice, if thrown, could make an impressive pile!

indicators.note: the last letter of the word one is taken
dice that are thrown tumble, so the letters of dice and if are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler hopes one final throw of the dice might win a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One last' gives E; 'thrown' rearranges DICE IF into DIFICE. 'Pile' here means a large building, not a heap or a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large imposing building, and a pile is a grand house or mansion.

clue.text: Two hacks, perhaps, will do for this tree!

parts.note: a hack is a riding horse, so the first hack is simply a horse
a chestnut is a horse of reddish-brown colour, another hack; it is also a stale old joke

explanation.surface: Two journalists, it is suggested, will be enough to identify this tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' suggests writers, but here both are horses: a horse and a chestnut. 'perhaps' warns these are examples.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse chestnut is a large tree bearing conkers, the shiny seeds children play with in Britain.

clue.text: Female supporter showing me fist, in rage

indicators.note: letters in a rage are thrown about wildly, so me, fist and in are reordered

explanation.surface: An angry woman shakes her fist at someone in support of her cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rage' rearranges ME FIST IN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of women's rights and equality of the sexes is someone backing a female cause.

clue.text: Ring tennis ace about uncompromising attitude

indicators.note: about means moved around, so all the letters of ring tennis ace are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis ace is phoned about a stubborn stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call or a tennis ring, but it is just fodder; 'about' rearranges RING TENNIS ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to change one's position or agree to anything is a stubborn, inflexible stance.

clue.text: Tree needing oxygen to survive

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
to survive is to live on

explanation.surface: A tree can only stay alive if it gets oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean evergreen grown for its fruit and oil.

clue.text: Man and wife taking article to Scottish islander

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, a man
a bride is a woman on her wedding day, a new wife
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A married couple take an item to someone living on a Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man and wife' looks like one wedded couple, but each word is a separate piece, and 'taking' just adds the article at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are island groups off the west coast of Scotland, so a native of them fits.

clue.text: Ten men sit around in judgement

indicators.note: around signals the letters of ten men sit are moved about

explanation.surface: Ten men sit around a table to reach a verdict, like a jury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges TEN MEN SIT; the jury picture makes 'judgement' sound legal, but it means an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or opinion held, a judgement in the sense of what one thinks.

clue.text: Here in France her majesty appears more frigid

parts.note: ici is the French for here
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen arrives in France and seems rather chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, meaning colder or more frosty.

clue.text: Stuff duck into puff-adder

parts.note: stuff is an old word for cloth or woven material
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a duck into a snake, a grotesque kitchen scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning fabric. Clotho is an old genus name for the puff adders as well as one of the three Fates.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho was once the scientific genus name of the puff adder, a venomous African snake.

clue.text: Where to get fruit or vegetables

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable, and chards are vegetables

explanation.surface: Advice on whether to buy fruit or vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is taken as written; the surface offers a choice, but 'Where to get fruit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, a place where apples and pears are grown and picked.

clue.text: Demoniac sort of wit

indicators.note: sort of here means a re-sorting, so the letters of demoniac are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fiendish kind of sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' looks like a hedge, but it signals a re-sort of DEMONIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A wit is a person who makes clever jokes, as a professional funny man does.

clue.text: Lingo tad faulty?

indicators.note: faulty signals the letters of lingo tad are wrongly placed and must be put right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a language is slightly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' rearranges LINGO TAD; the whole clue also defines the answer, a lingo that is a bit wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog Latin is mock or badly constructed Latin, a language that is somewhat incorrect.

clue.text: Set out carrying consignment — one mollusc, from Paris

indicators.note: the scrambled set holds the consignment piece inside it, as a vehicle carries a load
out means put out of order, so the letters of set are rearranged

parts.note: a cargo is a consignment of goods

explanation.surface: Someone sets off carrying a delivery: a single snail, from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' suggests departing, but 'out' scrambles the word set to EST, and 'carrying' places the load between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French word for an edible snail, a mollusc as eaten in France.

clue.text: Knock everybody out, briefly, with Italian port

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock
all means everybody
out abbreviated to its first letter gives O

explanation.surface: A boxer knocks everyone out, quickly, at an Italian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock everybody out' reads as one act of violence; it splits into three pieces, the last shortened by 'briefly' to a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapallo is a resort town and harbour on the Ligurian coast of Italy.

clue.text: S African wide-boy Eliot is to get rejection

parts.note: T.S. Eliot, the poet, gives his initials TS

indicators.note: rejection here means being turned back, so the words is and to are read backwards

explanation.surface: A South African hustler named Eliot is due to be turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get rejection' turns the two little words round to OTSI, placed after the poet's initials. 'Wide-boy' is British slang for a flashy small-time crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsotsi is a young street criminal or gangster in South African townships.

clue.text: Can key game of tennis go ahead in this location?

indicators.note: go ahead puts the tennis piece in front of the others

parts.note: a set is a unit of play in a tennis match
a tin is a can
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a crucial tennis match can go ahead here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb asking permission, but it is the noun TIN; 'key' is the musical key G.
explanation.definitionFit: A setting is the place where something happens, its surroundings or location.

clue.text: Fellow I'm taking up, astride donkey, to the peaks

definitions.note: a massif is one compact group of mountains, so the singular covers many peaks

indicators.note: astride means sitting with legs either side, so the reversed piece straddles the donkey
in a down clue taking up means lifting the letters so they read bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: taken as written
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A chap mounts a donkey to ride up into the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' turns the fellow and I'm upside down to MIF in this down clue, and 'astride' sets that round the donkey like a rider's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a block of high summits.

clue.text: Vagabond sometimes harboured?

explanation.surface: A wanderer who now and then finds shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A tramp steamer is a cargo ship with no fixed route, which only now and then puts into a port.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond is a homeless wanderer, while a tramp ship roams without a schedule and is in harbour only at times.

clue.text: At any rate, when at sea, seal is wet

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters of seal is wet are mixed

explanation.surface: When it is in the sea, a seal gets wet, anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges SEAL IS WET; the surface states the obvious about a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is an old-fashioned word meaning at least or anyway.

clue.text: Throw nine right next to the bull

definitions.note: a phrase describing the ring that stands for the noun

indicators.note: throw means toss about, so the letters of nine are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A darts player throws for nine just beside the bullseye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' scrambles the number to INNE; on a dartboard or archery target the inner is the ring just round the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target, the ring immediately surrounding the bullseye is called the inner.

clue.text: Waves when one of the French set off

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Waves when one of the French set off (9)' for UNDULATES: UN (one) + DU (of the) + LA + TES (set off) needs 'the' twice, for DU and for LA, and no reading found gives LA from 'when'
annotationWithheld.clue: Waves when one of the French set off

clue.text: Coin I tossed is of classical Greek design

indicators.note: a tossed coin spins, so the letters of coin and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: I flip a coin with a classical Greek pattern on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges COIN I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the three classical orders of Greek architecture, with scrolled capitals.

clue.text: Plump body, not taking account of small change

definitions.text: not taking account of small change

explanation.surface: A chubby figure who ignores the loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a number rounded off, such as a price quoted without the pence.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump shape is rotund in build, and a sum rounded to the nearest whole ignores the small amounts.
